per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a session, not an object

retention.stated: none: 'We do not offer persistent storage of any sort'

egress.terms: outgoing bandwidth limited to about 1 mbit per session

interface_detail: a Git repository is built into a Docker image and served as a JupyterHub session
tooling: any repo with a requirements.txt or environment.yml; the launch URL is the interface
chaining: a reproducible demo environment for a repo, not a place to compute: one CPU-hour and no disk

limits.value: 1 CPU-hour per session, or 6 hours of wall clock
about 1 mbit/s of outgoing bandwidth per session
0 days: no persistent storage at all

binding_note: one CPU-hour is reached in an hour of real work, and there is no disk to keep the result on

identity_cost.detail: no account and no card: a Binder link runs straight from a public repository. The service logs IP addresses for 30 days for abuse detection.

reliability_note: the project states it has no dedicated funding and runs on donated cloud, and it caps launches from most cloud providers
confidence_note: memory, session length, bandwidth and the absence of storage are all quoted from the project's user guidelines today.

shape.note: 1 GB guaranteed, 2 GB maximum; CPU is bounded in cpu-hours rather than cores

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 0.00: donated infrastructure, no paid tier
extras.unattended_mechanism: none: the session is bound to the browser and to the one-cpu-hour budget

session_cap.note: 6 h or 1 CPU-hour, whichever comes first; no persistence

extras.units: RAM and disk are quoted in the vendor's own decimal GB, not GiB. The ram_gib and disk_gib keys carry the vendor's number unconverted, so where a vendor writes 30 GB the key holds 30 and the true value is about 27.9 GiB. No conversion was performed.

free_tier.stated: free and unauthenticated: at least 1 GB RAM with a 2 GB maximum, up to 6 hours of session time or 1 CPU-hour, whichever comes first; no persistent storage of any sort
free_tier.notes: The governing limit is one CPU-hour, so six hours of session is only available to an idle kernel.

evidence.proved: quoted, emphasis markers in the original: 'users are guaranteed *at least* 1GB of RAM, with a *maximum* of 2GB'
quoted: 'Binder aims to provide up to six hours of session time per user session, or up to one cpu-hour for more computationally intensive sessions.'
quoted: 'We do not offer persistent storage of any sort, to protect us from becoming a host for malware.'
quoted, with the code span preserved: 'We limit outgoing bandwidth per-session ( `~1mbit`) to protect against being used as a DDoS vector.'
quoted, bold markers in the original: '**The maximum number of simultaneous users for a given repo is 100**.'

notes: The only anonymous provider, and the only one with a published CPU-hour cap that small. RAM is the project's own 'GB'; whether that is GB is not stated.
